pulses.name: merge-pipeline-landing
pulses.expect: at least one commit landing on origin/main within 6h

pulses.name: mergeloop-loaded
pulses.label: com.dear-agent.mergeloop
pulses.expect: the mergeloop launchd job to be loaded

pulses.name: otel-receiving
pulses.expect: Jaeger alive and receiving traces within 24h

pulses.name: absence-alarm-heartbeat
pulses.expect: an absence-alarm tick within 30m (3 missed 10-min launchd intervals)

pulses.name: merge-gate-not-systemically-failing
pulses.expect: no single required check failing across 30%+ of the open pull-request queue

pulses.name: retro-lint-guards
pulses.expect: all retrospectives within 7d declare valid guards or tracked deferrals

pulses.name: sandbox-gc-tick
pulses.expect: a COMPLETED sandbox-gc run within 2h (hourly job, 2 missed intervals). The evidence is the stdout log, which agm writes only after the run finishes, so a GC that errors early (for example a failed live-session inventory) leaves this stale and the pulse alarms. That is deliberate: a GC that never completes is a real problem a human should hear about, and remediation that cannot fix it reaches the give-up threshold and escalates. It does NOT prove the GC reaped anything (ce-uxju), and it does not distinguish 'not invoked' from 'invoked and failed' (ce-820tx).

pulses.name: token-refresher-tick
pulses.expect: a token-refresher audit append within 1h. file_mtime, not json_timestamp: the audit log is JSONL and the json_timestamp probe decodes only the first value in the stream, which is the OLDEST record (2026-06-19 on this host) and would alarm forever. Proves the refresher runs and writes evidence, not that the refresh succeeded.
